summary.text: 西 is the character for “west.” One traditional analysis treats the whole graph as a bird’s nest and links the western direction to birds roosting as the sun sets; the graph’s origin and the route to this meaning remain disputed.

formation.text: A disputed pictographic analysis reads 西 as a whole image of a bird’s nest, not as separable modern components. Another proposal derives its shape from an early form borrowed from 囟. The western-direction meaning may have been borrowed for a similar-sounding word or developed from the sunset-and-roosting association; the evidence does not resolve these accounts.

history.text: Graphic records identify oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal stages. The selected seal-script form is a modern reconstruction; the available accounts do not describe a detailed sequence of stroke changes.
One proposal says an early form borrowed 囟 because the words sounded alike in ancient Chinese, then developed into the 西 shape. This proposed graphic history is not settled.

uncertainties.text: The nest interpretation and the proposal involving 囟 remain competing accounts. Within the nest interpretation, it is also unresolved whether “west” came from reusing the graph for a similar-sounding word or from the sunset association. A bag or basket interpretation is mentioned, but its basis is unclear.
No supported name or pronunciation for a depicted nest, bag, or basket is available to explain the directional use as a sound-based borrowing from that object’s name.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: 西 is reported for the western direction in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. No individual dated examples establish a precise first use.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: The graph is also reported in place and palace names in these inscriptional periods. Their order relative to the directional use is unresolved.

“Nest” is proposed as the referent of the pictographic analysis, and one graphic-history account describes it as an original meaning no longer in use. This is not established as the earliest attested single-character use.

limitations.text: The accounts do not establish whether the western-direction use arose by borrowing the graph for a similar-sounding word or through a semantic association with sunset and roosting. No individually dated examples establish the sequence.

overview.text: 西 means “west.” One traditional reading sees the whole graph as a bird’s nest and connects west with birds roosting at sunset. The graph’s origin and the path to “west” remain disputed.
